chunks: And it is narrated from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
That Ali عليه السلام used to require the mukatab to continue working, because they did not used to stipulate that if he became unable, then he would be a slave.
And Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said: "They have their conditions."
And he عليه السلام said: "The mukatab is awaited for three installments; if he is unable, he is returned as a slave."

key_terms.رَقِيقاً: as a slave, in bonded status
key_terms.يَسْتَسْعِي: to require him to keep working and earning toward payment
key_terms.ٱلْمُكَاتَبَ: a slave under a contractual agreement of emancipation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a mukatab who cannot complete his manumission payments?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal ruling of the mukatab, a slave under a manumission contract. It indicates that contractual conditions are binding, and that a mukatab may be given up to three installments to fulfill the agreement; if unable to do so, he returns to the state of bondage.
